first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, so simplifying onboarding directly addresses both observed failures. Verify the prior onboarding-shortening and signup-simplification results before committing, then run a guarded test to protect qualified-revenue quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard self-serve onboarding-shortening experiment, prioritizing the confirmed result that increased completion, reduced time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. This directly addresses the current completion and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Treat signup-field simplification as SMB-only evidence and monitor qualified revenue and retention closely because its prior activation gain came with a 1% retention decrease; do not generalize it beyond SMB.

final2.rationale: The competitor’s deeper SMB price cut and doubled price-sensitive churn create an immediate retention and qualified-revenue threat. Run a tightly targeted promotional-pricing test for price-sensitive SMB prospects and at-risk accounts, with strict eligibility, duration, margin, conversion, retention, and qualified-revenue guardrails. This pivots from onboarding because the new evidence indicates urgent competitive pricing pressure, while preserving the onboarding test for a later cycle.
